Hi John / Sara --

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can make progress on the RAG proof-of-concept:

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: accurate, grounded answers for customer support KB + product docs (latency target: <= 600ms p95 for single-shot Q/A).
- Dataset: ~250k docs, mixed short & long (product guides + policy docs).
- Success metrics: grounding precision, answer helpfulness (human eval), token cost per request.

Initial recommendations (models & retrieval)
- Generator model candidates: rlhf-tuned large variants for quality -- try redwood-13b-8k (best quality) and redwood-6b-8k-quant (cost-sensitive).
- Embeddings: text-embedding-3-large for initial vectorization (good tradeoff of accuracy/cost).
- Retriever: HNSW index on FAISS with doc chunking @ 500 tokens, top_k=20 for recall.
- Reranker: cross-encoder reranker-v1 (costly but improves grounding precision). Use as a second-stage reranker to reduce hallucinations.

What we can run for you
- Out-of-box benchmark: Redwood can run a batch eval using your sample prompt set to measure grounding precision, helpfulness, and token economics.
- Deliverables: CSV of per-example metrics, recommended prompt templates, and suggested retrieval+reranker config.

Attachments I’m sharing
- prompt_set_v1.jsonl (small sample of your QA prompts)
- acme_rag_benchmark_template.csv (template for metrics)

Proposed next steps
1) Please confirm a sample dataset (5-10k examples) we can use for the initial benchmark.
2) We’ll run a 48-72 hour evaluation and share results + config recommendations.
3) Schedule a technical deep dive (solutions + infra) to review retrieval settings and reranker tradeoffs.

If that sounds good, I can block time for a deep dive next week -- two slots: Tue 3/9 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 3/10 14:00-15:00 PT.

Hi John / Sara --

Quick answers to the technical Qs:
1) Reranker cost/latency: using a cross-encoder on top_k=20 then re-scoring top 5 typically adds ~80-150ms per request (depending on instance class) and increases token compute cost by ~2-3x for the reranker step. To reduce cost while preserving precision we recommend:
   - offline candidate pruning (use a light bi-encoder to cut top_k to 10 before cross-encoding)
   - run reranker only for queries where top-1 similarity < 0.78 (confidence threshold)
2) Pass/fail grounding threshold: for the PoC target, aim for grounding precision >= 85% and human helpfulness >= 4.0/5 on a 200-example blind eval. These are conservative starting targets; we can iterate.
3) VPC/private eval: yes -- we can run the eval in a Private deployment or in a dedicated VPC-hosted job. We’ll need an approved IP allowlist and an S3 bucket or secure upload endpoint.

Other notes:
- Retrieval settings: chunk size 400-600 tokens works well for your doc mix; we recommend overlap 50 tokens for context continuity.
- Embedding refresh cadence: daily for docs that change frequently; weekly batch for static content.
- Caching: enable prefix caching for common queries to reduce cost.

I’ll drop a short playbook link and the RAG-eval checklist in the shared Drive.

Regards,
